figures.caption: Figure 1: Comparison of existing DyTAG modeling paradigms. (a) TGNN-based methods encode textual attributes as input features and model temporal interactions with temporal graph encoders. (b) LLM-based methods leverage language models to reason over textual attributes and interaction contexts. (c) Multimodal learning methods encode heterogeneous information sources with modalityspecific modules and integrate them for representation learning.

Table 1: AP (%) for dynamic link prediction under transductive (tr.) and inductive (in.) settings. OOM means out of memory. The best and the second best results are marked as bold and underlined, respectively.
Table 2: Hits@3 (%) for destination node retrieval under transductive (tr.) and inductive (in.) settings. The best and the second best results are marked as bold and underlined, respectively.

Figure 2: Overview of PRISM. PRISM encodes textual attributes as semantic priors and extracts historical interactions as behavioral evidence. It then performs iterative cross-modal posterior refinement to progressively transform semantic priors into behavior-conditioned posterior states.
Figure 4: Hits@10 (%) results for destination node retrieval.
